overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 17
overview.text: In this lesson, you will discover the power of factoring to solve higher-degree equations. The Zero-Product Property guarantees that if the product of multiple factors equals zero, at least one of the factors must be zero. This converts a quadratic equation into two simple linear equations.
outcomes: Understand and apply the Zero-Product Property: $ab = 0 \iff a = 0 \text{ or } b = 0$.
Solve quadratic equations written in factored form $(x - p)(x - q) = 0$.
Factor out common monomial factors to solve equations like $3x^2 + 27x = 0$.
overview.teacherInsight: Caution students that the Zero-Product Property ONLY works when the expression is set equal to ZERO. If $(x - 2)(x - 3) = 6$, you CANNOT conclude $x - 2 = 6$ or $x - 3 = 1$; you must first expand, subtract 6 to get standard form $x^2 - 5x = 0$, and refactor.

content.html:
Interactive Zero-Product Property Solver

Adjust roots $p$ and $q$ for $(x - p)(x - q) = 0$. Observe how each factor produces an independent linear equation.

Root 1 ($p$):p = 3
Root 2 ($q$):q = -2
(x - 3)(x + 2) = 0
Factor 1: x - 3 = 0 ⇒ x = 3
Factor 2: x + 2 = 0 ⇒ x = -2
Solution Set: {-2, 3}

vocabulary.definition: If the product of two real numbers is zero, then at least one of the numbers must be zero: ab = 0 implies a = 0 or b = 0.
An expression expressed as a product of irreducible linear or polynomial factors.
The input values that cause an expression or function to evaluate to zero.

practiceQuestions.question: Find the complete solution set to the quadratic equation $3x^2 + 27x = 0$:
practiceQuestions.explanation:
From the official Eureka Math Exit Ticket Key:
Factor out the greatest common factor $3x$: $3x(x + 9) = 0$. By the zero product property, $3x = 0 \implies x = 0$, or $x + 9 = 0 \implies x = -9$. Solution set: $\{-9, 0\}$.

practiceQuestions.question: Why is the algebraic statement 'If $ac = 5c$, then $a = 5$' FALSE?
options: Because if $c = 0$, then $0 = 0$ is true for ANY real value of $a$, meaning $a$ does not have to equal 5.
Because 5 cannot be multiplied by a variable.
Because dividing by $c$ is always illegal under all conditions.
Because $a$ must equal 0 whenever $c$ is present.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Rearranging $ac - 5c = 0 \implies c(a - 5) = 0$. By the zero-product property, either $c = 0$ or $a = 5$. If $c = 0$, the equation holds true regardless of what $a$ is (e.g. $7 \times 0 = 5 \times 0$).

exitTicket.title: Lesson 17 Exit Ticket: Equations Involving Factored Expressions
exitTicket.prompt: Find the solution set to the equation 3x^2 + 27x = 0. Determine if each statement is true or false: (1) If a = 5, then ac = 5c; (2) If ac = 5c, then a = 5.
exitTicket.solution:
Equation: 3x^2 + 27x = 0 => 3x(x + 9) = 0 => 3x = 0 or x + 9 = 0 => x = 0 or x = -9. Solution set: {-9, 0}.
Statement 1: If a = 5, then ac = 5c is TRUE (multiplication property of equality).
Statement 2: If ac = 5c, then a = 5 is FALSE. If c = 0, ac = 5c becomes 0 = 0, which is true for ANY value of a, not just a = 5. (ac - 5c = 0 => c(a - 5) = 0 => c = 0 or a = 5).

guidedExercises.title: Example 1: Applying the Zero Product Property
guidedExercises.scaffolding: The Zero Product Property asserts: $ab = 0 \iff a = 0 \text{ or } b = 0$. Factor the quadratic before applying the property.

steps.label: Apply Zero Product Property to $(2x - 7)(3x + 4) = 0$
steps.explanation: Set each factor equal to zero.

steps.label: Factor $x^2 - 9x + 20 = 0$
steps.explanation: Find two numbers multiplying to 20 and adding to $-9$ ($-4$ and $-5$).

steps.label: Solve factored quadratic
steps.explanation: Both $x = 4$ and $x = 5$ make the expression zero.

guidedExercises.commonPitfall: Applying the Zero Product Property when the right side is NOT zero (e.g. $(x-1)(x-2) = 6$). You CANNOT set $x - 1 = 6$! You must expand, subtract 6 to get zero on one side, and re-factor.
